To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the protein kinase Msk1 is associated with, functionally dependent upon and required for the targeting of KMTA/MLL to its target gene promoters.
the Msk1 kinase physically associates with the KMTA/MLL complex and is required for its normal activity in regulating gene expression and epigenetic marks.
the KMT2a/MLL1 histone lysine methyltransferases and Msk1 protein kinases are functionally linked in the regulation of gene transcription.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the Msk1 kinase in the epigenetic regulation of selected developmental genes.
the role of protein phosphorylation in the regulation of epigenetic mechanisms, and in particular with the role of MAPK-activated kinases.
the role of the MAP kinase pathway in the epigenetic control of gene expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Msk1 and KMT2A are functionally linked, and that Msk1 is a key component in the regulation of H3Kme4 by the KMT complex.
the Msk1 kinase is a key regulator of KMT2a/MLL1 activity, which is essential for the regulation of HoxA cluster expression and haematopoietic differentiation.
the KMT2/MLL1 SET domain methyltransferase complex, and the MAP kinase Msk1 are functionally and physically associated, and that this association is required for the activity of both complexes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Msk1 is a novel component of the KMT2 complex and that it is essential for its function.
KMT2a/MLL1 regulates the activity of a large number of genes through the Msk1 MAP kinase signalling pathway.
the KMT2a complex is associated with Msk1, and that Msk1 knock down phenocopies the effects of KMT2a knock down.
The main takeaway from our work is that

KMT2a/MLL1, a key regulator of gene transcription, is associated with, regulated by and functionally dependent on the MAP kinase signalling cascade, which is a major pathway in the regulation of gene transcription.
the MAP kinase pathway is not just a signalling pathway for gene expression, it is also a chromatin-modifying pathway.
the KMT2 complex is associated with and dependent upon the MAP kinase pathway, and this may be relevant to the role of KMT2 complexes in cancer.
